issue.body:
This PR adds usage of `terms.order` field which was not tested before.
Additionally, it does a small code cleanup (`HashMap` -> `Map`, `HashSet` -> `Set`, `Arrays.asList` -> `List.of`).

Relates https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104847

body:
The change mostly replaces `HashMap` with `LinkedHashMap`.  This is significantly easier than rebuilding the parsing logic and sorting it within Transforms.  In theory, `PivotConfig`'s `AggregationConfig` has enough information to inform us that the result will be sorted. In practice, we'd only be building around that information to determine if we should use a `HashMap` (when the order is not specified) or a `LinkedHashMap` (when the order is specified).

It *feels* like we should just keep the results as close to what we would get if we used the same request data in a plain search request or a transform -> search request, so all API behave the same. With that mentality it makes sense (to me) to just have Transforms always maintain the order as what is in the search result, and the search code can figure out what order it wants to return.

issue.title: [Transform] return results in order

labels.name: Team:ML
labels.description: Meta label for the ML team

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
Currently, when Transform searches over aggregations, it stores the results in an unordered HashMap. This potentially rearranges search results.

For example, if a user specifies an order in a search request, the search response is in that order. But if the search request is embedded in a Transform request, then Transform response will not preserve the order and the result will look different.

With this change, Transform will always preserve the order of the search response. A search embedded in a Transform should behave as an unembedded search.

Closes #104847
